name: Infantile Cerebral and Cerebellar Atrophy with Postnatal Progressive Microcephaly
aliases: Progressive Postnatal Microcephaly with Cerebral and Cerebellar Atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Infantile Cerebral and Cerebellar Atrophy with Postnatal Progressive Microcephaly

criteria.description: Postnatal onset of progressive microcephaly confirmed by serial head circumference measurements
MRI evidence of progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Global developmental delay or regression in motor and cognitive milestones
Exclusion of other metabolic, infectious, or genetic causes of microcephaly and atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive postnatal microcephaly, MRI-confirmed cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, and developmental delay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always conclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive reduction in head circumference after birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on neuroimaging
pathognomonic.notes: MRI shows progressive volume loss in cerebral cortex and cerebellum
searchTerms: brain and cerebellum shrinkage on scan
loss of brain tissue seen on imaging

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

occasional.notes: Increased muscle tone may develop over time
Impaired coordination due to cerebellar involvement
Including nystagmus or reduced visual tracking

rare.notes: Involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures

laboratory: Exclusion of inborn errors of metabolism
imaging: MRI showing progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Reduced brain volume with enlarged ventricles and widened sulci
other: Progressive head circumference decline documented by serial measurements

distinguishingFeatures: Congenital onset with hypoplasia rather than progressive atrophy
Calcifications and other signs on neuroimaging
Pattern of brain injury on MRI differs

redFlags: Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Orphanet: Infantile cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with postnatal progressive microcephaly, ORPHA:402364
Kumar A, et al. Progressive microcephaly with cerebral and cerebellar atrophy: clinical and neuroimaging features. J Child Neurol. 2018.
